clue.text: Beast that can be chained

indicators.note: the following word is said to be capable of becoming something else, so its letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild animal that can safely be kept on a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast's name uses exactly the letters of CHAINED, so the clue is a neat self-description.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny Australian egg-laying mammal, an animal and so a beast.

clue.text: Measure approximate to pound

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
a close guess is an approximate one

explanation.surface: Instructions for estimating a weight to the nearest pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the unit of weight, but it is the verb meaning to shut animals in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound livestock is to impound them, shutting them inside a fenced pen.

clue.text: Straying miners made chalk marks for workers to follow

definitions.note: plural, because the emblem is two tools

indicators.note: things that stray wander out of their places, so the letters leave their order

explanation.surface: Lost pitmen chalk up signs so their fellow workers can find the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifteen letters of fodder become the communist emblem, crossed tools symbolising industrial and farm workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossed hammer and sickle symbol stood for the union of industrial and peasant labour under communism.

clue.text: Many 7s in this kind of town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a room where many people sleep, 7 being the sleeping partner
second meaning: a commuter town where people only sleep

explanation.surface: A town full of silent investors.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the 'sleeping' half of 7-down matters: a room full of sleepers.
explanation.definitionFit: A room of many beds is one sense; a commuter settlement where residents merely spend nights is the other.

clue.text: Pest I found in a high degree

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a nuisance despite an advanced qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as pests.

clue.text: The main things lost

parts.note: surface reading: the most important things that have gone missing; setter's reading: the main is the sea, so these are things lost at sea, floating wreckage

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means floating wreckage or cargo washed overboard from a ship, goods lost on the ocean.

clue.text: Nice where nurse can go in topless in France

indicators.note: one item is said to be able to go inside another
without a top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse

explanation.surface: On the Riviera at Nice, a nurse is allowed to sunbathe topless.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the French city but is just the adjective. SISTER without its head goes into FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Finistère is a département at the western tip of Brittany, a region in France.

clue.text: 1/6 of sheep?

indicators.note: the fraction line is read as one numeral wrapped around the other

explanation.surface: A puzzling fraction: one sixth of a flock?
explanation.walkthrough: The fraction line is not division here: the top number is written as a word wrapped around the bottom one as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or like sheep, from the Latin word for a ewe.

clue.text: One backing non-runner

parts.note: surface reading: a punter betting on a horse that does not race; setter's reading: someone financing a business they take no part in running

explanation.walkthrough: Racing language misleads: backing here is investment, and the non-runner is the person who does no managing.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner who puts capital into a firm but takes no active role in managing it.

clue.text: Agreement held by right of office

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it

explanation.surface: A deal kept in place by the legal entitlement to hold a post.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to a town's chief civic official and that person's position.

clue.text: Thoroughly pleasant clothing before female's 4

indicators.note: clothing goes around a body, so one word wraps the rest

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Nice clothes come before the woman's 4-down, a puzzle cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 looks like a reference to 4-down, but it is just the number, IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a complete and exhaustive way, covering every detail, which is what thoroughly means.

clue.text: Signs of knife in the back in 'Vile Bodies'

indicators.note: read from the back, so the letters run right to left
the answer is contained within the title's words

explanation.surface: A stabbing scene in Evelyn Waugh's novel Vile Bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of obelus, a printer's dagger mark, lies backwards across the novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger symbol used in printing, so these marks are pictures of a blade.

clue.text: Disease for a watery finish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a viral illness of dogs
second meaning: a water-based paint for walls

explanation.surface: An illness that ends with a damp death.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a canine viral infection and also a cheap glue-and-water paint used on plaster.

clue.text: Dry up and flag when about to speak

indicators.note: turned about, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: to flag a path is to pave it with flagstones

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker dries up and wilts just before addressing the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like the verb to tire, but it is to lay flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that evaporates turns to vapour and disappears, which is drying up.

clue.text: Arena where one marched without honour

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around another piece

parts.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A stadium where someone paraded without any medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside. OM is the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Houston Astrodome was a famous covered sports stadium, the first domed arena of its kind.

clue.text: Sound out about name of punishment

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it

explanation.surface: Someone sounds out what a punishment is called.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to legal penalties, as in a penal colony or penal code.

clue.text: Plundering pirate on day-shift

indicators.note: to shift is to move about, so the letters change position

explanation.surface: A buccaneer does his looting during the daytime shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Preying on others and seizing their goods, which is plundering in the noun sense.

clue.text: Now's day for a drink

indicators.note: one thing given for another takes its place

parts.note: the letter that is swapped out

explanation.surface: Today is the day to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'day for a' literally: D stands in for the A in TODAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot alcoholic drink made with spirits, sugar and water.

clue.text: Sweet surprise to miss opening time

indicators.note: missing its opening, so the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A lovely surprise is spoilt by missing the start time.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry case with a sweet filling is served as a dessert, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Immediately resolved: no alternative in north Europe

indicators.note: something resolved is broken down and reworked, so the letters are reorganised
having no such thing means those letters are taken away

parts.note: the word offering an alternative, to be removed

explanation.surface: A decision is made at once that there is no other choice in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means straight after that, at once, so it matches immediately as an adverb.

clue.text: Place of inspiration fired boy to uphold right

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding something up lifts it, so the letters read bottom to top while keeping another piece inside

explanation.surface: An inspired boy is fired up to stand for what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' here is breathing in, not a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is drawn in through the nose's openings, so they are where breathing in, literally inspiration, happens.

clue.text: Inspiration saves heading for big fall

indicators.note: saves in the sense of except, so the word lacks its head letter

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper's inspired saves are heading off a heavy defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saves' looks like a keeper's stops, but it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy downpour is a large amount of precipitation coming down, a big fall of rain.

clue.text: Point to big 15's initial lead

parts.note: 15-down is a little tart, so the big one is a tart; 'to' places the point before it

explanation.surface: Someone points to a big cross-reference and its first clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is an advantage given at the outset of a race, a lead held from the beginning.

clue.text: Air that's more usually seen in cheerleaders

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the front letter of each word is taken

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A tune most often heard from cheerleaders at a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is hidden inside the word cheerleaders, whose first half is the last fodder word.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or tune, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Tapestry shows missing yard

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so those letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A wall hanging reveals that a yard of it is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a woven wall hanging, named after the French town famous for making them.

clue.text: Well-dressed in bowls?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for being dressed up very showily
second meaning, taken literally: the way a pet's food is served

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out player on the bowling green.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowls suggests the lawn game, but it is the dish a pet eats from; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom describes someone wearing flashy, overdone clothes; literally it is a pet's meal, served in a bowl.

clue.text: Support provided bysettler

indicators.note: the answer is said to be supplied by the following word's letters, made from them afresh

parts.note: the source runs 'by' into the fodder; the word to rearrange is settler

explanation.surface: A pioneer gives help to a new community.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs and a crossbar used to hold up a table top.

clue.text: Almost fool goblin command

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a troll is a goblin-like creature

explanation.surface: Tricking a goblin is almost an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Control is authority or mastery over something, the power to give orders.
